verdict_reason: Synthetic self-test case: one implementation commit (tag d03); the obvious fix (drop retired items, or hide them for everyone) breaks a documented rule.

implementation_commits.subject: Hide retired equipment from members; sort the list by name
implementation_commits.what: listEquipment filters retired items for members only and sorts by name; a test

docs_must_read.why: retired items stay in the registry; members do not see them, admins do; keys are slugs
the handler is where member and admin differ

files_edit.symbol: members do not see retired equipment; admins do

must_know_rules.rule: Retired equipment stays in the registry with retired: true; lists for members hide it, lists for admins show it
must_know_rules.why: the request reads like 'remove the old items', which would also hide them from admins

must_know_rules.rule: Equipment is keyed by its slug; never key a map or a lookup by the display name
must_know_rules.why: sorting and grouping by name invite a map keyed by name

must_know_rules.rule: Only the handler checks permissions: a member may change only their own reservations; an admin may change any
must_know_rules.why: the member and admin views differ in the handler, not in the registry

correct_approach: In listEquipment, keep the items for admins and filter out retired ones for members, then sort by name; leave the registry unchanged. Add a test for both views.

wrong_approaches.approach: Delete retired items from the registry, or filter them in registry.all()
Hide retired items for admins too
Build a map keyed by the display name to sort or deduplicate

stage2: a plan that filters retired items in the registry is flagged against docs/equipment.md:8

request_en: Members see old equipment we no longer use in the booking list and try to book it. Also the list comes in a random order; show it alphabetically.
notes: Self-test case. The snapshot and implementation are tags of the demo repository built by selftest/make_demo_repo.sh.
